text:
Maya: quick RFC follow-up: I built a tiny prototype of a 'mediator' service to centralize canary/AB cutover decisions and escape-hatch logic. goal: keep router simple and push orchestration into mediator.
Sanjay: ok, what minimal state does mediator need? sticky sessions? heavy KV?
Maya: minimal: per-canary short-lived lease, recent failure window, counters for probes. runtime keeps KV cache and model affinity; mediator only issues routing decisions.
Eli: does this create a new critical path / SPOF?
Maya: we plan HA leader election with readonly replicas. router has fallback: if mediator unavailable, it uses conservative local defaults (global fallback model, stricter rate limits).
Tess: ops asked for a manual emergency escape. can we support a force-fallback toggle?
Maya: yes. operator toggle with TTL and audit logging. toggle flips decisions to FORCE_FALLBACK until TTL expires or manually cleared.
Liam: where do SLO signals come from for automatic fallback?
Maya: mediator subscribes to the telemetry bus: p99 latency, error%, token-cost spikes. simple rule engine decides transitions. e.g. if p99>300ms or errors>2% over 5m -> shift 50% -> probe -> if probe fails -> full fallback.
Sanjay: can policies be per-tenant? we don't want one global knob.
Maya: policy blobs are per-tenant with inheritance from global defaults. config stored via gitops and can be patched in the console.
Eli: need idempotency for operations. otherwise a crash could double-apply traffic moves.
Maya: mediator issues opaque op_ids. router applies decisions idempotently and stores last_op_id per-route.
Tess: will this add latency to requests?
Maya: no. data path is still router->runtime. router reads an in-memory decision cache, atomic read is hot path (<200ns). mediator only controls control-plane transitions.
Liam: rollout plan? I'd prefer staged rollout with feature flag.
Maya: proposed rollout stages: 1) read-only mediator that only observes; 2) soft-suggestions (router logs but doesn't apply); 3) hard-decision for small tenant subset; 4) gradual expansion with automated rollback triggers.
Sanjay: rollback triggers should classify signals by origin (model-quality vs infra). different mitigations needed.
Maya: agreed. signals are tagged. policy actions: switch to alt model, reduce concurrency, shift region, or full fallback.
Tess: security and compliance? mediator controls routing so we need RBAC and signed operator actions.
Maya: mediator integrates with console RBAC and KMS for operator actions; every toggle emits audit events to logging.
Liam: how do we prevent flapping when telemetry oscillates?
Maya: state machine includes hysteresis, cooldown windows, and exponential backoff on probes. minimum dwell time between mode changes.
Eli: implementation surface? keep it small: gRPC service with tiny API.
Maya: MVP gRPC API: GetDecision(route, session_id) -> Decision(op_id, mode, reason) and ReportProbeResult(op_id, result).
Sanjay: good. also ensure a healthcheck and /metrics endpoint for alerts.
Maya: yes. next steps: I'll sketch a short design doc with sequence diagrams and prototype read-only mediator this sprint. tagging @Sanjay and @Eli for infra/runtime integration.
deploy-bot: created epic ARCH-2247 "Mediator-based fallback orchestration" and linked this thread.
Sanjay: :thumbsup:
Eli: :+1:
Tess: please add runbook steps for force-fallback and emergency unblock.
Maya: will add operator runbook and HA checklist to the doc and ping infra for deployment plan.
